stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 5 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 3 \) for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). At time t = 0 the particle is at \( \theta = 0 \), and its angle increases at the constant rate \( \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{8} \). Using a calculator, find the time t at which the x-coordinate of the particle's position is 6. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The angle starts at 0 and grows at a constant rate, so \( \theta(t) = \frac{\pi t}{8} \). The coordinate is \( x = r\cos\theta = \left(5 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 3\right) \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \), so in terms of time \( x(t) = \left(5 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{8} \right)} + 3\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{8} \right)} \).
Solve \( \left(5 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{8} \right)} + 3\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{8} \right)} = 6 \) on \( 0 \le t \le 4 \) with a calculator. The only solution is \( t \approx 1.480 \).

options.derivation: r treated as the x-coordinate, so the time at which r equals the value is reported
the equation solved in theta and the angle reported in place of the time
the angle rounded to one decimal place before it was converted to a time
